notes: Rule: 'When the SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph is specified, but computer-name-1 is not specified, the computer upon which the source unit is being compiled is the source computer.' (cite.py --check 12.3.5.4 -> OK §12.3.5.4 3)). Grammar: SOURCE_COMPUTER DOT ((computerName debuggingModeClause? unrecognizedClause?)? DOT)? — computer-name-1 optional, second period optional. Since computer-name-1 is never consumed, a name-less paragraph yields the compiling host as source computer, same as a named one. conformance:cases/12.3.5-SOURCE-COMPUTER/pb78_object_computer_optional_name compiles a name-less 'SOURCE-COMPUTER.' but is a test of OBJECT-COMPUTER, so it is not cited as closing this row. Whether a name-less SOURCE-COMPUTER is correctly gated/accepted at 1985 was not verified here (outside this GR's content). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (name-less paragraph form per the 2023 format; the '85 format required computer-name, see the grammar comment)] EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED 2026-11-10: in force at 85, §1985:VI.4.3.4 GR3 'When the SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph is specified, but the source-computer-entry is not specified, the computer upon which the source program is being compiled is the source computer', the name-less paragraph being a program of the 1985 format (§1985:VI.4.3.2 'SOURCE-COMPUTER. [ computer-name [ WITH DEBUGGING MODE ] . ]': the whole entry is bracketed), so the registrar remark above that the '85 format required computer-name holds only inside that optional entry.
